families.title: Inversion-recovery T1 mapping with radial readouts
families.input: A numerical object, prescribed inversion times, a radial sampling contract, and scanner hardware limits.
families.output: An exported sequence, Bloch-simulated measurements, reconstructed images, a T1 map, and reusable reconstruction and fitting code.
families.verification: Exported timing and trajectory, independent Bloch replay, T1 accuracy, and reconstruction and fitting on unseen inputs.
families.summary: I would like a simulated T1-mapping experiment on a numerical test object: an inversion-recovery acquisition with a radial-spoke readout.

families.title: Gradient-echo EPI with delay-robust reconstruction
families.input: A numerical object, EPI timing and sampling requirements, hardware limits, and a gradient-delay model.
families.output: An exported sequence with any required reference echoes, simulated measurements, and an image-reconstruction program.
families.verification: Timing and sampling, independent Bloch replay, and image accuracy on unseen objects with unknown gradient delays.
families.summary: Design a single-shot gradient-echo echo-planar imaging acquisition, export it as a Pulseq file, simulate that exported file on the supplied numerical object with an established Bloch simulator, and reconstruct the image from the simulated measurements.

families.title: 3D MP-RAGE with tissue nulling
families.input: A numerical object, a target tissue T1, fixed readout and cycle constraints, and hardware limits.
families.output: An exported MP-RAGE sequence with a justified inversion time, simulated measurements, and a reconstructed 3D image.
families.verification: Waveforms and timing, steady-state tissue nulling, independent Bloch replay, and reconstruction on an unseen object.
families.summary: Design a three-dimensional MP-RAGE acquisition whose inversion time nulls tissue with a T1 of 0.78 s, export it as a Pulseq file, simulate that exported file on the supplied numerical object with an established Bloch simulator, and reconstruct the 3D image from the simulated measurements.

families.title: Spin-echo EPI diffusion acquisition and ADC mapping
families.input: A numerical object, diffusion and spin-echo requirements, a diffusion model, and hardware limits.
families.output: An exported diffusion sequence, simulated measurements with b-matrices, an ADC map, and a reusable fitting program.
families.verification: Waveforms, spin-echo timing and b-matrices, independent simulation replay, and ADC accuracy on public and unseen objects.
families.summary: Design a single-shot spin-echo echo-planar diffusion acquisition with one b = 0 volume and three diffusion-weighted volumes, export it as a Pulseq file, simulate that exported file on the supplied numerical object with an established Bloch simulator using the diffusion model stated in task.json, and fit an apparent-diffusion-coefficient map.

families.title: Interleaved spiral acquisition and reconstruction
families.input: A numerical object, gradient and slew limits, sampling coverage requirements, and a recorded-delay model.
families.output: An exported spiral sequence, simulated measurements, and a reconstruction program that handles the recorded gradient delay.
families.verification: Integrated trajectories and coverage, independent Bloch replay, and image accuracy on unseen objects with gradient delays.
families.summary: Design an interleaved spiral-out gradient-echo acquisition under the stated gradient and slew limits, export it as a Pulseq file, simulate that exported file on the supplied numerical object with an established Bloch simulator, and reconstruct the image from the simulated non-Cartesian measurements.

families.title: Multi-shot turbo spin-echo acquisition
families.input: A numerical object, prescribed refocusing angles and timing, echo-train requirements, and hardware limits.
families.output: An exported turbo spin-echo sequence, simulated echo trains, a reconstructed image, and reusable reconstruction code.
families.verification: Sampling and timing, echo phase and steady-state consistency, independent Bloch replay, and unseen-object reconstruction.
families.summary: Design a two-dimensional multi-shot turbo spin-echo acquisition, export it as a Pulseq file, simulate that exported file on the supplied numerical object with an established Bloch simulator, and reconstruct the image from the simulated measurements.

families.title: Ultrashort-echo imaging with half-pulse excitation
families.input: A numerical object containing short-T2 tissue, half-pulse pairing and radial coverage requirements, and hardware limits.
families.output: An exported UTE sequence, simulated paired measurements, a reconstructed slice image, and reusable reconstruction code.
families.verification: Echo time, pair slice profile and coverage, independent Bloch replay, short-T2 signal, and unseen-object reconstruction.
families.summary: Design a two-dimensional ultrashort-echo-time acquisition with half-pulse slice excitation and centre-out radial readouts, export it as a Pulseq file, simulate that exported file on the supplied numerical object with an established Bloch simulator, and reconstruct the image of the selected slice, including tissue with sub-millisecond T2.

families.title: Single-voxel metabolite quantification
families.input: Raw multi-coil spectroscopy transients, a water reference, tissue fractions, and relaxation and acquisition parameters.
families.output: NAA, total creatine and total choline concentrations, a spectrum-fit figure, and a reusable quantification program.
families.verification: All three concentrations against truth on public and unseen data with different tissue and acquisition conditions.
families.summary: Quantify brain metabolites from the single-voxel MR spectroscopy dataset described in task.json.

families.title: Event-related fMRI effect estimation
families.input: A BOLD time series, event timings, slice and volume timing, and realignment parameters.
families.output: Single-event percent-signal-change and positive-response z-statistic maps, with a reusable analysis program.
families.verification: Effect-size accuracy and the null z distribution, including reruns with different timings and noise properties.
families.summary: Analyse the rapid event-related functional MRI run described in task.json.

families.title: T2 and transmit-field mapping from imperfect echoes
families.input: A multi-echo spin-echo image series, region labels, and pulse timing with imperfect refocusing.
families.output: T2 and relative B1 maps on the input grid, regional mean T2 values, and a reusable fitting program.
families.verification: Map accuracy, low-B1 bias, regional values, and reproducible fits on public and unseen scans.
families.summary: Please produce T2 maps from a CPMG multi-echo spin-echo scan whose refocusing pulses are imperfect, and treat the problem the way a quantitative-MRI researcher would.

families.title: Quantitative susceptibility mapping
families.input: Multi-echo magnitude and scanner-scaled phase images, brain and region masks, and acquisition geometry.
families.output: Local-field and susceptibility maps, regional susceptibility relative to ventricular CSF, and a reusable pipeline.
families.verification: Map and regional-value accuracy against simulated truth, including a rerun with a different subject and acquisition.
families.summary: We have a 3D multi-echo gradient-echo head scan and need quantitative susceptibility maps, with the susceptibility of the deep grey-matter nuclei expressed relative to ventricular CSF.

families.title: Cerebral blood flow from pCASL
families.input: Alternating control and label images, an M0 reference, tissue T1 maps, and slice and labelling parameters.
families.output: A cerebral-blood-flow map in mL/100 g/min and a reusable quantification program.
families.verification: Grey- and white-matter flow by slice against truth, including reruns with changed timing and suppression settings.
families.summary: Quantify cerebral blood flow from the pseudo-continuous arterial spin labelling (pCASL) dataset described in task.json.

families.title: APT-weighted CEST mapping
families.input: CEST and WASSR image series, an unsaturated reference, frequency offsets, and saturation parameters.
families.output: A B0 map and an APT-weighted asymmetry map at 3.5 ppm, with a reusable processing program.
families.verification: Regional and voxelwise asymmetry and B0 accuracy on public and unseen acquisitions.
families.summary: Produce an amide proton transfer (APT) weighted CEST map from the single-slice dataset described in task.json.

families.title: Diffusion processing and a two-group comparison
families.input: Scanner-exported diffusion images, gradient directions, acquisition times, region labels, and group assignments.
families.output: Regional FA, MD and principal directions, group differences with confidence intervals, and a subject-processing program.
families.verification: Tensor metrics and directions against truth, recomputed Welch statistics, and reruns on unseen subjects.
families.summary: Please build a processing pipeline for a small two-group diffusion MRI study that goes from the scanner export to regional tensor metrics and a group comparison.

families.title: Diffusion tensor mapping from raw EPI
families.input: Raw diffusion EPI and navigator readouts, a B0 map, gradient-nonlinearity fields, and a diffusion gradient table.
families.output: FA, MD and principal-direction maps plus a corrected mean unweighted image on the undistorted grid.
families.verification: Geometry, ghosting, regional tensor metrics and directions against truth, with reruns on unseen acquisitions.
families.summary: Produce diffusion tensor maps from the raw echo-planar diffusion dataset described in task.json.

families.title: Fat fraction and R2* from multi-coil k-space
families.input: Raw multi-echo k-space, receiver noise, a transmit-field map, acquisition parameters, and the fat spectrum.
families.output: Proton-density fat-fraction and R2* maps, a field-map figure, and a reusable reconstruction program.
families.verification: Regional fat-fraction and R2* accuracy against truth, including reruns with different acquisition and coil settings.
families.summary: Reconstruct quantitative fat-fraction and R2* maps from the raw multi-echo gradient-echo dataset described in task.json.

families.title: Learned versus classical quantitative reconstruction
families.input: Fully sampled training subjects and undersampled test scans, with echo times, masks, and tissue labels.
families.output: A trained network, tuned classical baseline, both test reconstructions, and a comparison based on regional R2* and B0 accuracy.
families.verification: Subject-level data separation, sampled k-space consistency, downstream accuracy, and both methods rerun on unseen subjects.
families.summary: We need to decide whether a small learned reconstruction is worth adopting for accelerated multi-echo gradient-echo scans, and what matters to us is the quantitative output, R2* and the field offset (B0) in tissue regions, rather than how the images look. task.json describes the training and test data, the k-space and sampling conventions, the signal model, the exact downstream R2*/B0 region analysis, the comparison protocol and the file schemas.

families.title: CPMG design under RF and gradient limits
families.input: Sample properties, echo-train requirements, and numerical RF, gradient, and peripheral-nerve-stimulation limits.
families.output: An exported CPMG sequence, simulated echo trains, computed safety quantities, and a T2/B1 fitting program.
families.verification: Limits recomputed from exported waveforms, independent Bloch replay, and T2/B1 accuracy on unseen noisy samples.
families.summary: We need T2 values from a multi-echo spin-echo (CPMG) train that stays within our scanner's RF and gradient safety limits, and because the refocusing pulses will be imperfect we also need each sample's transmit-field (B1) scale.

families.title: Spiral imaging with off-resonance correction
families.input: A numerical object with a spatial B0 field, a dual-echo field-mapping scan, and sequence constraints.
families.output: An exported spiral sequence, simulated measurements, an estimated field map, and an off-resonance-corrected image.
families.verification: Waveform limits and coverage, independent Bloch replay, field and image accuracy, and reconstruction on an unseen object.
families.summary: I would like an off-resonance-corrected spiral imaging experiment on a numerical test object, run entirely in simulation.

families.title: Scan-rescan T2 study from k-space to statistics
families.input: Undersampled multi-coil scans, noise prescans, region labels, and an analysis plan for a study with one missing rescan.
families.output: Per-scan T2 maps and measurements, participant-level group statistics, repeatability estimates, and reusable analysis code.
families.verification: T2 accuracy, map-to-table consistency, prescribed statistics, and reruns on unseen scans and study tables.
families.summary: Attached are the raw data of a small scan-rescan study comparing T2 in a target region between patients and controls.

families.title: Study design from pilot cartilage T2 measurements
families.input: Synthetic test-retest and patient-control pilot measurements, quality flags, and two proposed study questions.
families.output: Repeatability and group estimates, study designs, sample sizes, enrolment targets, and a short plan.
families.verification: Quality exclusions, participant-level analysis, uncertainty, design-specific variability, and sample-size calculations.
families.summary: We plan two studies with knee cartilage T2 as the outcome and have collected pilot data on our own scanner (the pilot data are synthetic; task.json and the CSV files in public/inputs describe them).

families.title: Evidence audit and research proposal
families.input: A synthetic cardiac MRI study corpus and rules for evidence, research gaps, study design, and sample size.
families.output: An evidence audit and cited proposal with a supported research gap, endpoint, controls, and enrolment calculation.
families.verification: Claims and citations against the supplied corpus, gap and design rules, and sample-size arithmetic.
families.summary: Our cardiac MRI group needs to choose its next study. I would like a well-founded research gap and a study proposal built strictly on the supplied corpus of 35 study records on myocardial inflammation (synthetic; see task.json and public/inputs).

families.title: Trial reporting with traceable quantitative claims
families.input: Synthetic trial results, reporting rules, and an allowed bibliography.
families.output: An abstract, a Results section, and a claim ledger linking reported values and uncertainty to source entries.
families.verification: Endpoint coverage, units and precision, uncertainty, supported language, citation keys, and claim-to-text consistency.
families.summary: Please write up the results of our trial of an oral remyelinating study drug in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMYEL-52, synthetic data) accurately and without overstating anything. task.json and public/inputs (results.json, results_tables.md and refs.bib) contain the study description, the individual result entries and the reporting rules.

families.title: Methods and statistics review of an MRI manuscript
families.input: A synthetic imaging manuscript with labelled paragraphs and tables, review categories, and pass criteria.
families.output: A structured review and referee report with quoted evidence, issue categories, proposed fixes, and a recommendation.
families.verification: Detected methodological problems, exact supporting quotations, and false accusations of sound passages.
families.summary: A neurology imaging journal has asked for a methods-and-statistics review of the attached manuscript on deep-learning reconstruction of undersampled FLAIR* for assessing the central vein sign in suspected multiple sclerosis (the manuscript is synthetic; see public/inputs and task.json).
